 Raptors News Raptors’ Barnes set to return against the New York Knicks
 The Toronto Raptors get some good news ahead of tonight's matchup.
 November 15, 2026 November 15, 2026 Camden MacMillan Photo Credit: Kirby Lee
 The Toronto Raptors receive some reinforcement ahead of a big matchup with the New York Knicks.
 Head coach Darko Rajaković announced Sunday afternoon that Scottie Barnes is available tonight against the Knicks after missing the last four games with a groin strain. Kawhi Leonard and Toronto’s two-way players — Nate Bittle, Malachi Smith, and Kevin McCullar Jr. — are out for tonight’s game. The Knicks have a clean injury report.
 Barnes is averaging 23.5 points, 7.6 rebounds and 5.1 assists across eight games this season and his absence has left Toronto searching for consistent ways to maintain an offensive floor. After beating the Milwaukee Bucks without him, the Raptors have dropped three in a row.
 Editor’s Note: The Raptors are starting Immanuel Quickley, Ja’Kobe Walter, RJ Barrett, Scottie Barnes, and Collin Murray-Boyles 
 The most interesting question that Barnes’ return raises is who is going to slide back to the bench. Jakob Poeltl has traditionally started at center, with Collin Murray-Boyles coming off the bench as a backup. However the two have started alongside each other over the last few games, so who gets the boot? Against the Knicks, Poeltl struggles to match up and he leaves the Raptors exposed defensively. The Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns pick and roll simply presents a challenge Poeltl has been unable to solve. I wouldn’t be surprised to see Murray-Boyles retain his starting position, with Poeltl moving to the bench. That move would also allow Poeltl to spend more time alongside Jamal Shead, whose playmaking complements his screen-setting and finishing. The two have a mutually-advantageous relationship. 
 Immanuel Quickley (18.5 points per game) and RJ Barrett (22.3) have produced without Barnes, but to mixed results and their efficiency has taken a dive. Barnes’ return should help take some of the burden off them as they look to steal a win against their former team. Meanwhile, Alijah Martin and Jamison Battle have made the most of their increased opportunities, as both are averaging over 12 points per game and have been red-hot from three over that stretch. If they can maintain that outside shooting, it should help Barnes by giving him more room to operate as he eases back into the lineup.
 Barnes return provides a significant boost on both ends of the floor as Toronto looks to snap a 13-game losing streak against the New York Knicks that dates back to January 22, 2023.
 Tip-off is set for 6:00pm ET on TSN.
